question.prompt: What observable interaction opens the global search overlay from the header field so the overlay-active Escape branch can be exercised without inventing behavior?

options.label: Defer branch
options.detail: Defer the overlay-active Escape scenario until another source defines how the global search overlay opens.

options.label: Typing opens overlay
options.detail: Assume entering text into the focused field opens the search overlay.

options.label: Need source
options.detail: Another source is needed to define the overlay-opening interaction.

content.risk_rationale: The use-case description and PRD mention a search overlay, but no cited source explains how that overlay becomes active; without that trigger, an overlay-dismissal scenario and test would be speculative.

content.title: Invoke the global search field with Cmd/Ctrl + K
content.intent: Prove the documented keyboard shortcut moves focus to the global search field and exposes a visible focus indicator without requiring pointer interaction.
content.technique_notes: Applied a11y because the path is keyboard-only and the source requires focus indicators. Applied state/flow because the shortcut changes the field from unfocused to focused. Applied equivalence partitioning because keyboard shortcut entry is a distinct access path from direct focus. Risk-judged combinatorial strength was 2 because only user-reach applied, but no covering_array expansion was needed because this path has no multi-input combination space.

content.title: Dismiss global search focus with Escape when no overlay is active
content.intent: Prove Escape clears the active global search focus state when the field is focused and no search overlay is open, following the recommended branch of the unresolved Escape rule.
content.technique_notes: Applied state/flow because Escape changes the field from focused to unfocused. Applied equivalence partitioning because this covers the no-overlay branch of the ambiguous Escape promise. Negative and boundary techniques were not applicable because the source defines a dismissal transition, not invalid input handling or a numeric range. Risk-judged combinatorial strength was 2 because only user-reach applied, but no covering_array expansion was needed because the branch has a single state variable.

content.title: Inspect the header global search field before and after direct focus
content.intent: Prove the centered header search field shows the promised placeholder, gains the promised focus affordances, and keeps its 420px by 36px footprint when focused.
content.technique_notes: Applied equivalence partitioning because direct focus is a distinct entry path into the field. Applied state/flow because the path compares unfocused and focused field states. Applied responsiveness/layout-stability reasoning because the PRD promises the field remains visually stable when focused. Boundary value analysis was not applicable because the PRD gives fixed dimensions, not an input range. Risk-judged combinatorial strength was 2 because only user-reach applied, but no covering_array expansion was needed because there are no combinable variable inputs for this path.

judgements.rationale: [applicability] Kept a dedicated keyboard-path scenario because the shortcut focus promise is explicit in the PRD and materially different from direct pointer focus.

[applicability] Kept only the no-overlay Escape branch because the PRD states “Escape clears focus/search overlay” but does not define how to open the overlay; covering the focused-field branch avoids inventing an activation flow.
[applicability] Kept a direct-focus scenario because the PRD separately promises focus styling and visual stability whenever the field is focused, independent of keyboard shortcut entry.
